brief.overview: Blyth Town Council is seeking a contractor for the replacement and installation of ten bus shelters across Blyth, Northumberland. The project involves removal of existing shelters, site preparation, supply and installation of new shelters, and associated ancillary works. The works must be completed by 28 February 2027 and include one living roof shelter.

redFlags.description: Two readings of the pack disagree on: contract duration. Check these against the documents before relying on them.

citation.quote: The minimum public liability requirement for this tender is £5 million unless the tender documents state otherwise.

redFlags.description: Minimum public liability requirement is £5 million. This is a high level of cover that could be a barrier for some smaller suppliers.

citation.quote:
Decision / contract award | 26 October2026
Contract commencement | 26 October 2026

redFlags.description: The contract commencement date and contract award date are the same (26 October 2026), allowing no time between award and start for mobilisation or contract finalisation.

citation.quote: Tenderers must satisfy themselves that the information provided is sufficient to prepare a complete and fixed-price tender.

redFlags.description: Tender is required to be a 'fixed-price tender', but also to identify any proposed departures to Terms & Conditions, and any contract variation may affect the contract sum. This creates potential for conflict and price re-negotiation or risk.

citation.quote: The contractor shall tender a completion price in accordance with the pricing information and Schedule of Works.

redFlags.description: Tender is required to be a 'fixed-price tender' and 'The contractor shall tender a completion price'. This puts all price variation risk on the contractor.

citation.quote: Invoices paid | 15 March 2027

redFlags.description: Although it mentions 'statutory payment requirements include payment of valid and undisputed invoices within 30 days' for Procurement Act 2023, the timetable states 'Invoices paid | 15 March 2027'. This implies a single payment after completion, rather than interim payments, but the Tender Form states 'I agree that the contract sum may be paid by interim payments where provided for in the contract'. This creates an ambiguity regarding payment frequency.

citation.quote: I agree that the contract sum may be paid by interim payments where provided for in the contract and subject to the Council's payment procedures and applicable statutory requirements.

redFlags.description: The Tender Form mentions interim payments, but the Key Dates schedule suggests a single payment date after contract completion. This needs clarification.

citation.quote: The contractor should advise on a suitable site from these four locations, with consideration to the effects of coastal winds, birds and other site-specific concerns, and considering the other potential sites.

redFlags.description: Contractor must propose the suitable site for the living roof from 4 identified options, providing justification considering coastal winds, birds, and other site-specific concerns. This requires specific expertise and risk assessment in the bid.

citation.quote: As there is no shelter currently on the site, the utilities are not known and require investigation.

redFlags.description: For sites where no shelter currently exists (04 Tynedale Drive, 05 Regent Street), utilities are unknown and require investigation by the contractor. This adds an element of risk and potential for unforeseen costs/delays.

citation.quote: Directly in front of the shelter is a busy road between a roundabout and a railway level crossing.

redFlags.description: Some sites involve working on a busy road or narrow footpaths, requiring careful traffic and pedestrian management plans.

citation.quote: Metal mesh and side panels to be returned to Town Council for re-use.

redFlags.description: Metal mesh and side panels from existing shelters to be returned to Town Council for re-use. This requires careful handling and transport logistics, which must be factored into the bid.

citation.quote:
Briefly describe how you propose to carry out the works, including:
- Site surveys and pre-start checks
- Removal of existing shelters
- Site preparation and groundworks
- Installation of new shelters
- Resurfacing and making good
- Cleaning and completion

questions.draftText:
Site surveys and pre-start checks
We will carry out a measured site survey at each location to record dimensions, underground services and photographic condition records. RAMS will be prepared for every site and briefed daily, led by our Operations Manager (NEBOSH-qualified) prior to start [E3]. All site operatives hold CSCS and NRSWA Streetworks accreditation; supervisors hold SMSTS [E3]. [EVIDENCE NEEDED: confirmation of specific utility-locating subcontractor or in-house capability]

Removal of existing shelters
Existing shelters will be dismantled and removed, with materials segregated for reuse/recycling and waste transferred via a licensed carrier; waste transfer notes will be kept for each site, as in our Durham programme [E2].

Site preparation and groundworks
We will excavate to suit new foundations, install new concrete bases and make good levels. Works on the highway will be managed under Chapter 8 traffic management by our NRSWA-accredited operatives [E2][E3]. If contaminated material or unexpected services are found we will stop work and notify the contract administrator.

Installation of new shelters
Shelters will be assembled and fixed to new foundations following manufacturer instructions. We completed 14 cantilever shelters across six villages in 11 weeks, demonstrating our delivery approach and sequencing for multiple sites [E2]. [EVIDENCE NEEDED: confirmation of chosen shelter manufacturer and technical installation drawings]

Resurfacing and making good
Footway and surrounding surfaces will be reinstated to match existing materials where possible; no footway will be closed for more than one working day, as achieved previously [E2]. Any defects will be rectified within the defects period.

Cleaning and completion
On completion we will remove debris, provide handover documentation, as-built photos and waste transfer notes, and complete a client snag list; in Durham two minor snags were fixed within five working days and one warranty replacement was completed within 48 hours [E2].

evidenceGaps: confirmation of specific utility-locating subcontractor or in-house capability
confirmation of chosen shelter manufacturer and technical installation drawings

parts.note: Describes measured surveys, RAMS, daily briefs; staff accreditations claimed but unsupported.
Describes dismantling, segregation and waste transfer notes; previous Durham example unsupported in library.
Mentions excavations, concrete bases and Chapter 8 traffic management; NRSWA accreditation unsupported.
Explains assembly to manufacturer instructions; manufacturer choice and drawings not provided.
Promises reinstatement and limited footway closure; previous performance claim unsupported.
Lists handover documents and snags resolution; specific evidence from prior works not in library.

evaluation.rationale: Fair — the response addresses all requested sub‑parts with a clear sequence and some relevant practice (surveys, RAMS, segregation of waste, handover). However several claims lack supporting evidence or contradict the evidence library (eg staff qualifications, NRSWA/SMSTS, previous Durham programme) and two explicit '[EVIDENCE NEEDED]' placeholders remain. The answer is therefore thin on verified detail and gives only moderate confidence the requirement would be met.
strengths: Logical, end‑to‑end sequence covering all requested stages.
Includes practical details: RAMS, waste transfer notes, as‑built photos and snagging.
Commits to limited footway closure and prompt snag resolution which are client‑focused.

improvements.rationale: Scoring rewards supported claims; the library lists ISO 9001 and CHAS only, so cite those or supply certificates.
improvements.suggestion: Replace accreditation claims with documentary references from E1.

improvements.rationale: Specific evidence for service detection is critical; removes '[EVIDENCE NEEDED]' and increases confidence in safety.
improvements.suggestion: Confirm utility‑locating capability and name subcontractor or in‑house team.

improvements.rationale: Demonstrates preparedness and technical fit; directly supports installation sub‑part and raises score.
improvements.suggestion: Provide chosen shelter manufacturer and attach technical installation drawings.

improvements.rationale: Evaluation requires evidence of relevant experience; use verifiable examples to support delivery claims.
improvements.suggestion: Replace references to 'Durham programme' with documented project summary from E1.

improvements.rationale: Open placeholders undermine credibility; supplying proof converts partly to covered.
improvements.suggestion: Remove bracketed '[EVIDENCE NEEDED]' notes and include specific RAMS/NEBOSH proof.

improvements.rationale: Adds technical detail to groundworks and shows proactive risk management, improving score.
improvements.suggestion: State contingency steps for contaminated ground with specific testing method.
